examGuide.title: Mental model and derivation
examGuide.body:
Big-O is an upper bound and does not itself mean worst case; first specify which cost function is bounded. Theta needs both upper and lower bounds. Logarithm bases differ by constants. Nested-loop bounds cannot be multiplied blindly when inner work depends on outer state. Geometric decreases can yield linear sums despite logarithmic iteration counts. Auxiliary space includes simultaneous live storage, not all allocations ever performed.

**Key relationship:** 1+2+…+n=n(n+1)/2=Θ(n²)

examGuide.title: A repeatable solving procedure
examGuide.body:
1. Define input size and cost case.
2. Count the true iteration sum.
3. Compare dominant growth with justified bounds.

examGuide.title: Approach the exam question
examGuide.body: Separate best, worst and expected costs before choosing bounds. Big-O is an upper bound, not a synonym for worst case. Ratio limits establish little-o or Theta relations. Geometrically shrinking inner loops can sum to linear work despite logarithmically many outer iterations.

examGuide.title: Worked problem
examGuide.body:
For n=64, loops process n,n/2,n/4,…,1 elements. How many increments occur?

**Answer: 127.** The exact sum is 64+32+16+8+4+2+1=127=2n−1. Its order is Θ(n), not Θ(n log n), because the inner work shrinks geometrically.

examGuide.title: Conditions and edge cases
examGuide.body:
A constant number of Θ(log n) searches is still Θ(log n). Multiply loop bounds only when their product reflects actual work.

O(n²) is a valid upper bound for a linear function, but it is not a tight description.

examGuide.title: Worked question patterns
examGuide.body:
#### Pattern 1 · MCQ

1+2+4+…+n for power-of-two n is:

- **A.** Θ(n log n)
- **B.** Θ(n²)
- **C.** Θ(log n)
- **D.** Θ(n)

**Answer: D.** The geometric sum is 2n−1, so it is Θ(n).

#### Pattern 2 · MSQ

Choose valid asymptotic statements.

- **A.** n is O(n²)
- **B.** n² is Θ(n)
- **C.** log₂n is Θ(log₁₀n)
- **D.** n log n is o(n²)

**Answer: A, C, D.** A is a loose upper bound; logarithm bases differ by a constant; log n/n tends to zero. B fails the lower growth comparison.

#### Pattern 3 · NAT

For n=8, how many executions occur in for i=1..n, for j=1..i, increment?



**Answer: 36.** Count Σi from 1 to 8: 8·9/2=36, rather than multiplying n by n.

#### Pattern 4 · NAT · Transfer problem

For i=1,…,8, an inner variable j starts at 1 and doubles while j≤i, performing one increment each iteration. Total increments?



**Answer: 21.** For i=1..8 the counts are floor(log₂i)+1: 1,2,2,3,3,3,3,4. Sum=21. The inner bound depends on i rather than always equalling log₂8.

examGuide.title: Work through the supplied PYQs
examGuide.body:
#### GATE 2023 CS · Q29 · MSQ

[Open the original question and try it](/#/lesson/asymptotic-analysis?tab=practice)

**What is tested:** Asymptotic time and space complexity. Refer to the original image for complete givens and diagrams.

1. f(n)=n and g(n)=n² give f(n)/g(n)=1/n→0.
2. This proves f∈o(g), and little-o also implies f∈O(g).
3. A lower bound f∈Ω(g) fails because no positive constant times n² stays below n eventually. Consequently f∈Θ(g) also fails. Select **A,C**.

#### GATE 2024 CS1 · Q17 · MCQ

[Open the original question and try it](/#/lesson/asymptotic-analysis?tab=practice)

**What is tested:** Asymptotic time and space complexity. Refer to the original image for complete givens and diagrams.

1. A single pass performs at most a constant amount of work per adjacent pair, giving an O(N) worst-case upper bound.
2. An already sorted array, or an array whose violating pair occurs last, forces the algorithm to examine all N−1 adjacent pairs. That supplies an Ω(N) worst-case lower bound.
3. Thus the worst case is Θ(N), both bounds in **A**.
